findings.property: Program-input-repair-plan-v2 closed Python form prohibits the - stdin source mode and requires the selected pinned script to execute.
findings.evidence: scripts/task-run-guard.py interpreter_script consumes optional -- at lines 129-130 and then calls pinned_script without rejecting argv[i] == "-". If cwd contains a directly pinned regular file named -, argv [resolved_python, -I, -S, --, -] therefore passes validation. Python retains the special stdin meaning of a filename equal to -, including after --; with DEVNULL the interpreter can exit successfully without running that pinned file. General file checks and postcondition validation also accept the existing pinned file. This is a narrow incorrect admission and success case, not unpinned source execution.
findings.uncertainty: Established by source control flow and Python stdin-sentinel semantics. No additional runtime probe was executed because this review was restricted to the specified suite. The existing suite lacks the pinned literal-name - plus -- case.
findings.falsifier: Before any repair, add and execute a focused regression with valid pinned resolved Python -I -S -- -, a pinned regular cwd/- file containing a harmless marker, and valid policy/review controls. Require refusal78 before journal mutation or child dispatch. Preserve a healthy ./- or absolute-path script control and literal - after an ordinary script. Reject only the actual selected Python stdin sentinel; no generic parser change or reopening of DEVNULL is required.
